news.text: 14 May saw underdog underdogs **Wimbledon FC** script one of the most stunning upsets in football history by defeating reigning league champions Liverpool 1-0 in the **FA Cup final** at Wembley Stadium. Managed by Bobby Gould, the physical, long-ball "Crazy Gang" took the lead through a Lawrie Sanchez header before goalkeeper Dave Beasant etched his name in legend by saving a second-half penalty from John Aldridge—the first penalty save in FA Cup final history. As the final whistle blew, BBC commentator John Motson delivered the immortal line: "The Crazy Gang have beaten the Culture Club!"

news.text: 15 May saw the Red Army commence its official withdrawal of troops from **Afghanistan**, bringing an end to more than eight bloody years of military occupation. Operating under the terms agreed at the Geneva Accords, columns of Soviet armored personnel carriers and tanks began the long overland trek back north across the Amu Darya river toward the Uzbek border. Soviet commanders acknowledged the immense physical and psychological toll the protracted conflict had inflicted on their conscripts, who returned home to a rapidly transforming nation.

news.text: 15 May saw Scottish pop quartet **Wet Wet Wet** claim the number one spot on the UK singles chart with their soulful cover of the Beatles' classic *With a Little Help from My Friends*. Released as a charity double A-side alongside folk-punk bard Billy Bragg's rendition of *She's Leaving Home*, the single raised immense funds for the ChildLine telephone helpline for vulnerable children. Marti Pellow's smooth, earnest vocals carried the release to a dominant four-week residency at the summit of the British charts.

news.text: 27 May saw the British Parliament enact the controversial **Section 28** of the Local Government Act 1988, barring local authorities from "intentionally promoting homosexuality" or teaching the "acceptability of homosexuality as a pretended family relationship" in state schools. Championed by Conservative MPs and staunchly backed by Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher, the legislation provoked massive civil rights demonstrations and prompted direct action protests, including lesbian activists abseiling into the House of Lords chamber during debates.

29 May saw US President **Ronald Reagan** arrive in Moscow for an extraordinary diplomatic summit with General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev, becoming the first American president to visit the Soviet capital in fourteen years. Strolling arm-in-arm with Gorbachev through a sunlit Red Square while chatting warmly with ordinary Soviet citizens, Reagan was asked by a journalist if he still considered the USSR an "evil empire". The President smiled and answered without hesitation: "No, I was talking about another time, another era."
